text:
The tone of the original email is authoritarian, abrupt, and dismissive. It uses commanding language ("It's been decided without room for negotiation," "Make the necessary arrangements") which can create resentment and lower morale among employees. To match a more professional, respectful, and collaborative sentiment, the email should acknowledge the inconvenience, provide context if possible, and use polite, inclusive language.

Here is a suggested revision:

Subject: Update Regarding Weekend Overtime Requirements

Hi Team,

I am writing to inform you that we have a requirement to hold overtime hours this weekend. Due to current project demands, this schedule is fixed and cannot be adjusted at this time.

I understand this may require some personal adjustments on your part, and I appreciate your flexibility and commitment to getting this done. Please make the necessary arrangements to ensure you are available.

Thank you for your hard work and cooperation.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

***

Regarding your second request: Sugar, specifically sucrose, has a distinct sweet taste. It is one of the five basic tastes (along with sour, salty, bitter, and umami) and is perceived by sweet receptors on the tongue. The sensation is generally described as pleasant and rewarding, which is why it is widely used in food and beverages to enhance flavor and provide energy.
